newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LATE CLARIDGE GOAL SINKS WEARY MIDDLESBROUGH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE CLARIDGE GOAL SINKS WEARY MIDDLESBROUGH.

text.p: An extra time goal from striker Steve Claridge gave Leicester a 1-0 victory in the English League Cup final replay on Wednesday and wrecked Middlesbrough's dreams of lifting the first major trophy in their 121-year history,
Claridge, who put Leicester into the premier league with a last minute strike in a play-off at Wembley last season, volleyed home a Steve Walsh cross after 99 minutes of a tight cup tie.

Brazilian Emerson squandered a wonderful chance to equalise a minute later when he worked a 1-2 with Juninho, but Middlesbrough, wilting at the end of their third two-hour cup tie in 10 days, had nothing left to offer.
The victory gave Leicester their first major trophy since 1964 and only the second in their history.
It also put the mid-table Midlands side into Europe next season.
"We could be playing Barcelona," Claridge said afterwards.
"I don't know how fazed they'll be when they run out at (Leicester's ground) Filbert Street."
Middlesbrough, who were three minutes away from beating Leicester in the initial match at Wembley, must now lift themselves for their F.A. Cup semifinal replay against Chesterfield next Tuesday.
They also face a relegation scrap compounded by an energy sapping fixture schedule.
"We're obviously disappointed but that's the way Cup finals go sometimes," Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson said.
"Leicester rested their players at the weekend. We couldn't afford to do that as we had such an important match."
Wednesday's match was a closely fought affair which produced few clear chances.
Emile Heskey had the best effort of the first half. He beat Middlesbrough's stand-in keeper Ben Roberts but then saw his shot cannon off the post.
Middlesbrough's talented foreigners Emerson, Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli occasionally threatened to break the stalemate but were generally well shackled by the Leicester defence.
Then came extra time and Claridge's winner.
"When you get to extra time you've obviously got two very tired sides," Leicester boss Martin O'Neill said.
"Another five minutes and I don't think we'd have had three players still standing.

"The goal Steve scored for us at Wembley at the end of last season made all this possible. He's not had the best of seasons but that doesn't matter. We're in Europe and Europe means just about everything."
